item.title: Bridging Badiou's Gaps: Topos Theory and the Bodies of Mathematical Expression
item.description: arXiv:2611.27280v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This article develops a second stage of an argument begun in 2013, revisiting Alain Badiou's use of topos theory in Being and Event and Logics of Worlds. The previous article diagnosed Badiou's reduction of topos theory to its atomistic, localic form as the scientific scapegoat in his attack on 'democratic materialism'. Now I ask what follows when this logicist illusion is dispelled and the categorical alternative is taken seriously, particularly with respect to forcing, semantic expression, and mathematical subjectification that constitute the key elements of Badiou's earlier work. I thus reconstruct Badiou's own arguments in a corrected form, while transferring them to a categorical framework. The aim is not to introduce new mathematical results, but to identify what is conceptually lost through their reduction to set-theoretic formalism. In particular, I describe Cohen's forcing argument in the context of Grothendieck topoi and Kripke-Joyal semantics, thereby explicating the geometric structures implicit in Badiou's thinking. This reconstruction further brings into view a different way of understanding Badiou's concepts of subject, body, and change. Rather than treating a topos as merely a formal container for mathematical objects, I propose reading it as a body of mathematical expression, aligning with Johnstone's characterization of a topos as a 'universe of discourse'. At the same time, the geometrization of logic allows Badiou's own four-fold typology of change - when applied to topos theory itself as a mathematical 'event' - to be anchored to various historical definitions of a topos. In this way, the article bridges Badiou's two major works while clarifying how his own limited expression of mathematical formalism embodies his 'dialectical', ultimately singular concept of the event, and the way it clouds his philosophical understanding of locality and temporality.
item.dc:creator: Antti Veilahti

item.title: Lax-idempotent monads in homotopy theory
item.description: arXiv:2610.41904v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We extend the theory of lax-idempotent monads to the setting of $(\infty,2)$-categories. In particular, we prove an analogue of Kock and Z\"oberlein's characterization of the category of algebras over a lax-idempotent monad. We then apply this theory to many examples that arise naturally in homotopy theory. For example, we show that $(\infty,1)$-toposes are monadic over presentable $(\infty,1)$-categories, with left adjoint given by the symmetric $(\infty,1)$-topos. We also show that $\infty$-operads are comonadic over symmetric monoidal $(\infty,1)$-categories through the monoidal envelope construction, obtaining along the way a new proof of Barkan-Steinebrunner's result that the envelope functor is a faithful inclusion. We furthermore use this theory to simplify Ramzi's proof that dualizable stable $(\infty,1)$-categories are comonadic over $\aleph_1$-compactly generated stable $(\infty,1)$-categories.
item.dc:creator: Fernando Abell\'an, Thomas Blom

item.title: An Open Petri Net Implementation of Gene Regulatory Networks
item.description: arXiv:1907.11316v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Gene regulatory networks (GRNs) are a central object of systems biology, and many formalisms have been used to model them, among them Petri nets. Ordinary Petri nets, however, provide no built-in way to assemble a large network from smaller, separately specified pieces. Open Petri nets, in the sense of Baez and Master, supply exactly this: an open Petri net is a Petri net with designated boundary places, and open Petri nets are composed by gluing boundaries together (a pushout), giving a symmetric monoidal double category Open(Petri). In this paper we (i) state precisely the standard encoding of activation, inhibition and degradation as Petri net transitions; (ii) distinguish the classical "Petri nets are monoids" view of Meseguer and Montanari, which describes how processes inside one net compose, from the open Petri net view, which describes how nets compose; (iii) show, with a worked example, how a GRN can be cut into open Petri net modules along shared genes and recovered exactly by composition, together with simple rules that make such a decomposition correct; and (iv) use the compositional rate-equation semantics of Baez and Pollard to show that the mass-action dynamics of the composite network are obtained by gluing the dynamics of its modules, linking Petri net models of GRNs to their ordinary differential equation counterparts. We close by discussing what the reachability semantics does and does not give for GRN modules, and the limitations of the approach.
item.dc:creator: Yanying Wu

item.title: Semi-exact functors and the conjecture of Coulembier and Flake
item.description: arXiv:2611.24471v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We introduce the notion of semi-exact functors between abelian categories, which are characterised by either preserving or breaking exactness of sequences. We prove semi-exact functors are always exact with respect to a canonically determined exact structure. For a symmetric tensor category $\mathscr{C}$, we define a support theory by considering all $\Bbbk$-linear symmetric monoidal, semi-exact functors $\mathscr{C}\to\operatorname{Ver}_{p^\infty}$ up to equivalence, and conjecture that it agrees with the Balmer spectrum of the stable category when $\mathscr{C}$ is finite. We prove a weak form of this conjecture and other results for Tannakian categories and in characteristic 0. Critical to the positive characteristic case is a functor constructed by Coulembier and Flake who were interested in higher Frobenius functors. We show that their construction, which relies on the theory of abelian envelopes, gives a natural source for semi-exact functors, and at least in the Tannakian setting gives all $\Bbbk$-linear, symmetric monoidal, semi-exact functors.
